messages:
leo: thinking about a microprofile-driven lane split for the continuous batcher. build a tiny per-tenant profile (median seq len, small-request pct, burstiness score) and use that to pick packing vs isolated lanes. low-cost to compute and can adapt quickly.

tess: interesting. how would that interact with KV cache affinity? small requests often benefit from warm KV. if we move tenants around we might lose cache hits.

leo: yep that's the main risk. plan is to prefer local-worker packing when KV hit-rate > 70%. otherwise prefer isolation to avoid cold-kv penalties. store microprofile with last-seen-worker tag.
omar: what about model-variant heterogeneity? some tenants route to quantized variants which are faster but have different token throughput. mixing them in a packing lane could mis-shape batches.

leo: good call. include "variant_entropy" in profile. if entropy > threshold, don't pack with default fast-path; instead use a mixed-lane that pays a small scheduling tax.

riti: worried about synchronized rebalancing thundering herd. if many tenants move at once we could spike. propose randomized backoff and a probabilistic drift: only move 10% immediately, rest sampling over 30-120s.

leo: agree. also enforce min-residency 60s and a move-penalty counter that increments on repeated moves (exponential cooldown).
tess: metrics we need: packing_fill_ratio, per-tenant_local_kv_hit, variant_entropy, lane_move_rate, move_penalty_count. also surface per-worker skew so controller can see hotspot nodes.

omar: admission control detail: keep per-worker fast-path local decision based on recent microprofile + a tiny credit counter (pack_credits). credits accrue slowly, consumed on enqueue to packing. eviction from packing costs extra credits.

leo: credit math: accrual = base_rate * (1 + small_request_rate). This rewards tenants that consistently send small requests. cap credits to avoid hoarding.

riti: how do we handle large occasional requests? e.g., tenant mostly small but sometimes asks for 2k tokens. Want to avoid long headroom mis-estimates.

leo: add a size_hard_hint on enqueue and allow a one-shot bypass to isolation; if size_hard_hint > worker_threshold then bypass packing. also treat large request as a temporary negative sample for the microprofile.
tess: tracing: every enqueue should tag lane_decision={reason:microprofile|kv|variant|manual,score:X,worker_local:true}. makes debugging easier.

omar: rollout: telemetry-only for 48h, then small canary of 5 tenants across three workers, then widen. instrument a synthetic client that emits small p95 targets to validate tail.

leo: reconciliation: local fast-path, occasional global reconcile every 20s that recomputes thresholds using aggregated microprofiles. controller can nudge unhappy tenants.

riti: one more: think about model cold-start cost on GPU when moving tenant to isolation lane. we might need a soft-warm step where we prefetch KV and model weights for a few seconds before live traffic.

leo: yes prewarm hook makes sense. add prewarm_budget metric to avoid thrashing GPU memory.

ci-bot: deployed experiment flag scheduler.microprofile_lanes=true to canary cluster-5; metrics pipeline enabled.

tess: great. i'll add the metric names and dashboard panels. watch packing_fill_ratio, variant_entropy, and 99.9 for interactive endpoints.

omar: i'll prototype the local credit allocator focusing on eviction penalties and cap logic.

leo: thanks all 680 i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with API shape for enqueue hints: {target_lane: "auto|pack|iso", size_hint:int, variant_tag:string}.

riti: postmortem pre-req: if packing_fill_ratio drops >30% after rollout, auto-disable and dump microprofiles.

leo: noted. reconvene in 24h with first telemetry.
